tool_findings.message: Function definition does not bind loop variable `user`
Function definition does not bind loop variable `subject`

findings.title: Late-binding closure captures loop variables
findings.explanation: The lambda defined in the loop captures the variables `user` and `subject` by reference. All callbacks will use the values from the last iteration, sending emails to the wrong recipient and subject.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind the current values in the lambda default arguments, e.g., `reminders.append(lambda u=user, s=subject: send_email(u["email"], s))`.
findings.verdict_reason: The lambda defined inside the for-loop closes over `user` and `subject` variables, which are mutated each iteration, causing all callbacks to use the final iteration's values.

evidence.why: lambda captures loop variables by reference

findings.title: Potential email header injection via user-provided name
findings.explanation: The subject line is built directly from `user['name']` without any sanitisation. If the name contains newline or other header‑control characters, an attacker could inject additional email headers when `send_email` constructs the message.
findings.suggested_fix: Sanitize or escape the user-provided name before inserting it into the email subject, e.g., remove newline characters or use a safe formatting library.
findings.verdict_reason: The send_email function does not build or send actual email messages; it merely prints the subject, so user-provided names cannot inject email headers.

evidence.why: send_email only prints the subject, not constructing email headers
no sanitisation or header handling performed

findings.title: Lambda captures loop variable
findings.explanation: Using a lambda inside a loop captures the loop variable by reference, so all callbacks will send to the last user instead of the intended one. This is a common Python pitfall and will cause incorrect behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a default argument or a helper function to bind the current user, e.g. "reminders.append(lambda u=user: send_email(u['email'], subject))".

findings.title: Unvalidated email address may lead to injection in email sending routine
findings.explanation: `send_email` is called with `user["email"]` taken directly from input data. If `send_email` builds a command line or email headers from this value, a malicious email address could result in command injection or header injection.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the email address format and escape any characters that could be interpreted by the email-sending implementation before passing it to `send_email`.
